title: Trump Commuted Mark Shapiro’s 85-Year Prison Sentence to Time Served
description_short: On Dec. 23, 2020, Trump commuted Mark Shapiro’s 85-year prison term to time served, leaving restitution and supervised release in force.
description_medium: On December 23, 2020, Trump commuted Mark Shapiro’s 1,020-month prison sentence to time served. The warrant says a jury returned a guilty verdict on November 23, 2009, and states that continued confinement was unnecessary to the ends of justice through his projected 2078 release date and release would not compromise community safety. It left three years of supervised release, $22,075,631 in restitution, and a $500 assessment intact.
description_long:
On December 23, 2020, Trump commuted Mark Shapiro’s 1,020-month (85-year) prison term to time served. The clemency warrant identifies his Southern District of New York case, says a jury returned a guilty verdict on November 23, 2009, and leaves a three-year supervised-release term, $22,075,631 restitution, a $500 special assessment, and other sentence components in force. It states that continued confinement was unnecessary to the ends of justice through his projected August 31, 2078 release date and that release would not compromise community safety.

A March 2006 U.S. Attorney’s Office announcement described charges arising from Cobalt Capital real-estate companies. It said the criminal complaint alleged Cobalt raised about $16 million from more than 150 investors and that funds were used for undisclosed loans to Shapiro and a co-defendant, personal expenses, construction at Shapiro’s home, and jewelry and vehicles. The complaint also alleged investor materials misrepresented Shapiro’s operating role and omitted prior convictions; about $214,000 was allegedly transferred toward his prior fraud restitution. These are complaint allegations, not findings described in the announcement, which explicitly said defendants were presumed innocent unless proven guilty. The warrant independently records the later conviction and commutation.

https://www.justice.gov/pardon/page/file.publisher: U.S. Department of Justice, Executive Grant of Clemency
supported_facts: The warrant identifies Mark Shapiro’s Southern District of New York conviction and says a jury returned a guilty verdict on November 23, 2009.
The warrant recites a 1,020-month (85-year) prison term, three years of supervised release, $22,075,631 restitution, and a $500 special assessment imposed October 21, 2010.
The December 23, 2020 grant commutes the prison sentence to time served and leaves restitution, the assessment, supervised release, and other sentence components intact.
The warrant states its rationale as the ends of justice not requiring continued confinement to the projected August 31, 2078 release date and community safety not being compromised by release.

source_excerpts.quote: WHEREAS MARK SHAPIRO, Reg. No. 13354-014, was convicted, in the United States District Court for the Southern District of New York on an indictment (Docket No. $1:06-CR-357-01 (KMW)) of violations of Sections 78j(b) and 78ff, Title 15, United States Code, and Sections 371, 1341, and 1343, Title 18, United States Code
the jury returned a verdict of guilty on November 23, 2009
I commute the prison sentence imposed upon the said MARK SHAPIRO to time served.

I leave intact and in effect the remaining unpaid balance, if any, of the $22,075,631 restitution obligation, the special assessment of $500, the three-year term of supervised release with all its conditions, and all other components of the sentence.

I commute the prison sentence imposed upon the said MARK SHAPIRO to time served. I leave intact and in effect the remaining unpaid balance, if any, of the $22,075,631 restitution obligation, the special assessment of $500, the three-year term of supervised release with all its conditions, and all other components of the sentence.

it has been made to appear that the ends of justice do not require the said MARK SHAPIRO to remain confined until his currently projected release date of August 31, 2078, and the safety of the community will not be compromised if he is released
do hereby grant clemency to the said MARK SHAPIRO
I, DONALD J. TRUMP, President of the United States of America

https://www.justice.gov/pardon/page/file.limitations: The warrant’s OCR corrupts its final date line; the December 23, 2020 event date is retained from the supplied DOJ table observation. The warrant gives no further account of clemency deliberations.

https://www.justice.gov/archive/usao/nys.publisher: U.S. Attorney’s Office, Southern District of New York
supported_facts: The March 27, 2006 announcement says the criminal complaint alleged Cobalt raised roughly $16 million from more than 150 investors.

The complaint alleged investor funds were used for undisclosed loans and personal expenses, including construction related to Shapiro’s residence and expenses paid from a Shapiro-controlled trust account.
The complaint alleged investor materials described Shapiro as a consultant and omitted his actual operating role and prior convictions.
The announcement says approximately $214,000 of Cobalt investor funds were transferred as partial payment of restitution from Shapiro’s prior bank- and tax-fraud convictions.
The announcement expressly cautions that the complaint’s charges were accusations and defendants were presumed innocent unless proven guilty.

source_excerpts.quote: Cobalt has allegedly raised more than approximately $16 million from more than approximately 150 investors.
They are alleged to have used investor funds to make undisclosed loans to SHAPIRO and STITSKY, and to pay for personal expenses of SHAPIRO, STITSKY and FOSTER.

approximately $2.2 million of Cobalt funds were transferred to a trust account, not affiliated with Cobalt and under the control of SHAPIRO, which was then used to pay SHAPIRO’s personal expenses, including payments for jewelry and vehicles.
One of the documents provided to the investors described SHAPIRO as a consultant
The charges contained in the complaint are merely accusations, and the defendants are presumed innocent unless and until proven guilty.

https://www.justice.gov/archive/usao/nys.limitations: This announcement summarizes allegations in the criminal complaint, not adjudicated findings about each transaction. The clemency warrant independently confirms Shapiro’s later conviction in the matching SDNY case.
